articles.title: ‘Intelligent caller’ to team leader: How this call centre ran Apple gift card scam
articles.summary: Gurgaon police busted a call centre posing as Apple support, arresting 17 for scamming US/Canada iPhone users via pop-ups, remote access and $500–$1,000 gift cards.
articles.body: GURGAON: An alleged cyber fraud operation that cheated iPhone users in the US and Canada by impersonating Apple customer service representatives was busted on Thursday, with the arrest of 17 people, including five women, from a commercial office in Sector 61. Police said the operation had a structured hierarchy of callers, a team leader, a firm director and an operator referred to as the “intelligent caller”.The accused allegedly sent pop-up alerts to iPhone users claiming that a charge of $5,000 had been imposed on their Apple accounts, and asked them to call a number to get it cancelled. Police said call-centre employees received these calls through the MicroSIP application and spoke to victims in English. They told victims that their Apple accounts had been accessed by someone else and that technical assistance was needed to secure them.“After gaining the victims’ confidence, the accused persuaded them to download remote access applications on their phones. Through these, the accused obtained access to the victims’ phones and collected their information, including names, addresses, email IDs and other important details. Subsequently, the victims were told that additional security was required to protect their accounts and were asked to pay for the gift card,” an officer privy to the investigation said.Victims were persuaded to buy Apple gift cards worth between $500 and $1,000 each. The card numbers were shared with the alleged main operator, Chirajuddin Ashrafi, a resident of Delhi’s Laxmi Nagar, who is absconding. The defrauded amount was received through gift cards and cryptocurrency.The officer said the operation had designated roles. Nitesh, an MBA graduate, was allegedly the group’s “intelligent caller”, Aneesh was named as a director of the firm in its rent agreement, and Sukhdeep Singh allegedly functioned as the team leader.“Nitesh would put a stamp on the successful fraud. Aneesh would manage the entire space, while Sukhdeep managed the callers,” the officer added.All 17 arrested were aged between 25 and 30. Most were Class XII passouts, while some were graduates in philosophy, BCom and BA. The investigation indicated that employees were paid between Rs 30,000 and Rs 50,000 a month, apart from commissions.“The call centre operated under the name Sigma Tax from the 18th floor of M3M Digital Green building on Golf Course Extension Road, in units 1818 and 1819,” the officer further stated. Police said the network had earlier operated from Delhi before shifting to Udyog Vihar, where it ran for around six months. It had been operating from the M3M premises for the past two months.ACP (Cyber) Gaurav Fogat said police received information about the illegal call centre on Wednesday evening. A team from Cyber Crime South police station, led by Inspector Dinesh, raided the premises and arrested 12 men and five women.Police seized 17 computers, six laptops and five phones. “A Land Rover Defender with a temporary registration number, allegedly used by arrested accused Shazia Khan, was also taken into possession. Khan, a resident of DLF Phase 3, Sector 24, originally hails from Lucknow,” the ACP said. Police suspect she may be an important link to Ashrafi.Police are examining the seized devices to establish the number of calls made and victims cheated, the total amount involved and the network’s financial trail. “Technical analysis of the software, internet-based calling applications, remote access tools and other digital evidence being used on these devices is being carried out. Through this analysis, information is being gathered regarding other persons associated with the network, the actual amount of fraud, identities of foreign victims and transactions involving the defrauded money,” Fogat said.“Even five successful calls per caller could indicate a substantial volume of fraud, with each Apple gift card worth $500,” he added.A case has been registered under sections 318(4) (cheating), 319 (impersonation) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of BNS and sections 43 (damage to computer), 66 (computer related offences), 66D (cheating by personation by using a computer resource) and 75 (offence or contravention committed outside India) of Information Technology Act.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: RSM Classic: Billy Horschel faces setback over PGA Tour future after slow start, as Jesper Svensson races ahead
articles.summary: Sweden's Jesper Svensson holds a one-shot lead after the opening round of the RSM Classic, the final PGA Tour event of the season; Brooks Koepka is five strokes back and Billy Horschel is seven behind; watch the second round live on Friday from 1.30pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Only the top 100 in the FedExCup standings after this week's event in St Simons Island remain fully exempt on the PGA Tour, with Horschel heading into the week 101st and projected to fall further down the rankings after opening with a one-under 71.

Horschel - an eight-time winner on the PGA Tour - carded three birdies and two bogeys on the Plantation Course, one of two used at Sea Island Golf Club, to leave him seven strokes behind Svensson.

Svensson birdied eight of his last 11 holes on the same course as Horschel - including each of his last four - to post an eight-under 64 and move into a one-shot lead, with Max Greyserman and Garrick Higgo sharing second after opening 65s.

Michael Thorbjornsen posted the lowest round on the Seaside Course, with a six-under 64 leaving him tied-fourth alongside Emiliano Grillo, Hank Lebioda, Maverick McNealy, Lee Hodges and Davis Riley.

Ramsus Hojgaard and Marco Penge, entering the week outside the top 100 in the season-long standings, sit in the group on four under alongside Ryder Cup player Sepp Straka - who finished inside top 50 during the regular season.

Koepka described his season as a "disappointment" ahead of this week's event, with the five-time major champion opening with a three-under 67, while England's John Parry - entering the week 96th in the ranking - started with a two-under 70.

All players ranked No 51 and below carry their FedExCup points over from the regular season and first play-off event into the 'FedExCup Fall', giving them the chance to boost their status for next season.

Those 51st to 60th after this week qualify for the first two Signature Events of 2027, while those who end between 101st and 125th on the PGA Tour only receive conditional status and be unable to feature in certain events.

Players outside the top 125 face a season on the Korn Ferry Tour or a trip to Q-School to earn their PGA Tour playing rights, with first-round leader Svensson entering the week in 135th spot.

Who will win the RSM Classic? Watch throughout the week live on Sky Sports. Live coverage continues Friday with Featured Groups from 1.30pm on Sky Sports Golf ahead of full coverage from 5pm. Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract .

articles.title: LPGA Tour: England's Charley Hull one stroke off lead at lucrative season finale
articles.summary: England's Charley Hull cards a six-under 66 to sit one shot off the first-round lead at the LPGA's lucrative season-ending CME Group Tour Championship.
articles.body:
CME Group Tour Championship - round one leaderboard

7 K Davidson (Aus), AL Kim (Kor), J Thitikul (Tha); -6 C Hull (Eng

Selected others: -6 L Coughlin (US), A Kim (US), P Roussin-Bouchard (Fra); -5 Y Noh (US), L Woad (Eng), G Lopez (Mex), C Boutier (Fra) -4 N Korda (US), C Ciganda (Spa); -2 L Maguire (Ire)

England's Charley Hull carded a six-under-par 66 to sit one shot off the first-round lead at the LPGA's lucrative season-ending CME Group Tour Championship.

Australia's Karis Davidson, South Korea's Kim A-lim and Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul, set the pace at seven under at the Tiburon Golf Club in Naples, Florida.

World number two Thitikul, who is aiming to win the event for the third consecutive season, responded to a bogey on the 12th hole by knocking in five consecutive birdies on the back nine.

Hull, who triumphed a decade ago, is one of nine players a stroke behind the leading trio on a stacked leaderboard that contains the top 60 in this season's points list, who are all chasing the $4m (£3.05m) top prize.

"When I won 10 years ago I didn't really take golf seriously. I remember coming into this event when I won, hungover," Hull said.

"I felt pretty good [today]. I kind of like lost my swing feels [at the] end of last week because my hip was very tight, and it just like started rerouting my golf swing," Hull said.

"Today I was nervous on the first tee. I felt like I had no swing feeling. Then as the round developed I felt like I hit it really nice."

Hull's compatriot Lottie Woad made six birdies and a bogey as she signed for five-under 67, along with France's Celine Boutier.

World number one Nelly Korda, who will qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame if she wins on Sunday, endured a mixed day but picked up shots on the 17th and 18th as she finished on four under.

With an $11m purse on offer, Korda would also break Annika Sorenstam's career earnings record if she finishes in sixth place or better.

The Swede amassed 10 major titles and earned $22,583,694 during a storied career before retiring in 2008, with Korda now just under $160,000 behind that mark.

articles.title: Digboi Golf: Three-way lead at top after Round 3 sets up exciting final day
articles.summary: DIGBOI: Yuvraj Singh joined overnight leaders Om Prakash Chouhan and Raunil Kukar at the top as the 26th Indian Oil SERVO Masters Golf tournament looks
articles.body: DIGBOI: Yuvraj Singh joined overnight leaders Om Prakash Chouhan and Raunil Kukar at the top as the 26th Indian Oil SERVO Masters Golf tournament looks poised for an exciting final day at Digboi Golf Links with a three-way lead for the title after the third round here on Thursday.Overnight joint leader Chouhan (67-68-70), 40, carded a two-under 70 – with six birdies, a double-bogey on the par-3 10th and two bogeys – to retain his share of the lead.The 28-year-old Kukar (70-65-70), from Bengaluru, the other overnight joint leader, also returned a two-under 70 comprising five birdies and three bogeys to remain at the top.Kapurthala’s Yuvraj (68-70-67), 25, who began the day tied fourth and three shots off the lead, fired a five-under 67 featuring seven birdies and two bogeys to join the overnight leaders. He made six of his birdies in two sets of three consecutive holes, first from the fifth to seventh and then from the 14th to 16th.Bangladesh’s Md Razu (69-70-68) climbed from tied eighth to fourth at nine-under 207 following a four-under 68 with five birdies and a lone bogey on the par-4 eighth.The biggest jump of the day belonged to Mumbai’s Aryaman Aditya Mohan (73-70-65), who climbed from tied 25th to tied fifth at eight-under 208 with a seven-under 65 featuring an eagle on the par-5 seventh, eight birdies and three bogeys.Chandigarh’s Akshay Sharma (75-67-66) joined Aryaman in tied fifth after a six-under 66 comprising an eagle on the seventh, six birdies and two bogeys.However, the title looks to be former champion Chouhan’s to miss continued to put himself in contention for another title.“I played well today. My putting was good as well, although I struggled a little with my putting tempo on the 10th hole,” Chouhan said of his third-round show.The 11-time PGTI winner, former European Challenge Tour winner and 2023 PGTI rankings champion, however, said he would do the planning for the final day only after waking up on Friday.“It depends on my mood and the vibe after I wake up in the morning. If I worry about it from now on, I won’t be able to sleep tonight,” he told TOI.Kukar, playing his sixth consecutive PGTI season, came close to his maiden title at Nava Raipur Open in September, where he finished joint runner-up, one shot behind Khalin Joshi.Kukar, who made a bogey on the final hole along with Chouhan, said, “OP and I both made bogeys on the last hole, which was unfortunate, but we have to take things as they come. I’m very grateful to be where I am right now. There is still a lot of work to do and a few things to prepare for tomorrow.”Yuvraj, playing his fourth consecutive PGTI season, will be chasing his maiden title with his current best finish on the tour being the third place at PGTI Players Championship in April 2025.“It feels good to be at the top of the leaderboard. I think what worked for me today was simply sticking to my process and doing what needed to be done,” said the 25-year-old.The undulating fairways and small greens at Digboi Golf Links have tested the field and will be ready with challenges on Friday to crown the winner of this Rs 1 crore prize money event.(The writer is in Digboi on an invitation from DP World PGTI)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Smith’s Tour Path Reveals PGA’s Hard Rules On Exemptions
articles.summary: Cameron Smith faces a strict wait to return to the PGA Tour. Brian Rolapp explains why no special deals exist for LIV players.
articles.body:
A curious detail has emerged regarding Cameron Smith's path back to the PGA Tour, and it highlights a major sticking point for the league. The Australian star secured a lifeline to play in the DP World Tour, but his route to the American circuit remains blocked by strict regulations. According to Fox Sports, Smith and other former LIV players must wait until one year passes after their last LIV event before they can compete on the PGA Tour again. For Smith, Bryson DeChambeau, and Jon Rahm, that date lands on August 26, 2027.

PGA Tour chief Brian Rolapp has made it clear that the organization will not bend these rules for specific individuals. He recently stated that while fans want the best players together, the tour operates as a membership organization with rules designed to ensure fairness. "Rules matter and they will be enforced," Rolapp said following the unveiling of the new structure commencing in 2028. This stance effectively ends hopes for a quick return via a special exemption, a path the tour briefly opened at the start of 2026 for a select few.

While Rahm and DeChambeau have a guaranteed spot in the 2028 Championship Series due to their recent major wins, they still need a place to play this season. Smith does not have that same automatic guarantee and must navigate the waiting game while finding other tournaments. Fox Sports, accessible via Kayo, is the sole venue to view the Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia live, providing Smith a current competitive spot. Patrick Reed successfully won back his card in 2026 by playing strong golf in Europe during his cooling-off period, and Smith must now follow that same route.

Rolapp compared the future of golf to the growth seen after the ABA-NBA merger and the NFL-AFL merger. He told the Sports Business Journal that the sports business is not that difficult if the product is competitive. "The sports business is not that difficult," said Rolapp at SBJ's Dealmakers event in Manhattan on Wednesday morning. He argued that if the tour gets the best competitive product, fans will reward it with their time and attention, which drives the commercial success.

The tour is looking to boost media value by creating scarcity with a new Championship series. Rolapp noted that the old model with 47 events diluted the fields and confused viewers. The new plan aims to deliver a clear value proposition from the Super Bowl through the end of August. Rolapp believes media rights will continue to rise as money moves away from scripted programs and into live sports events. "It'll go up because more and more money will be reallocated from scripted program and other things that are more commoditized into sports live events," he said. However, he warned that this shift does not mean media money will feed everything the tour needs.

While the big names like Smith wait, other players are fighting for their careers right now at the RSM Classic. Neal Shipley starts the week ranked 123rd and needs to finish in the top 125 to keep his status. Shipley, who has risen from No. 183 following the regular season, stated "If I just take care of my business, I think I will be just fine," The stakes are high for everyone in the field, as the top 100 earn full status and players ranked 101-125 get conditional status for the 2027 season.

Chad Ramey proved that winning the right event can change a career overnight. "My life kind of went from very uncertain of what I'm going to be doing in January to now I kind of know what I'm doing the next two years," Ramey said. The FedEx Cup Fall determines eligibility for signature events next year, making every stroke count for players like Chandler Phillips who are battling to lock up their cards.

articles.title: Koepka Admits Scheffler’s 2024 Dominance Would Have Faced LIV Challenge
articles.summary: Brooks Koepka reflects on Scottie Scheffler's historic 2024 season, admitting the LIV Golf stars would have put up a fight against the PGA Tour leader.
articles.body:
Scottie Scheffler has built a legacy of dominance on the PGA Tour, securing 22 victories since his first win in February 2022. A common critique suggests these wins came easier after top rivals like Brooks Koepka departed for LIV Golf. That narrative faces a direct challenge from the five-time major champion himself. Koepka, speaking while still competing on the Saudi-backed circuit, offered a candid assessment of Scheffler's 2024 campaign. He acknowledged that the world number one delivered a performance that stands as one of the greatest in tour history, regardless of the field strength.

The conversation took place back in 2024, a time when Koepka and other stars had already moved to LIV Golf. According to HITC , Koepka was asked specifically about Scheffler's season during that period. The former world number one did not shy away from the topic. "Scottie had a hell of a year," Koepka admitted. To contextualize the achievement, he went further, stating, "I think it's arguably one of the best years the tour has ever seen." This comment highlights the sheer volume of success Scheffler achieved even without the full depth of the 2021 or 2022 fields.

Koepka also weighed in on Bryson DeChambeau's form during that same season, noting that the American golfer played significantly better than he did. "Bryson had a hell of a year too – he played 10 times better than I did," Koepka said. He added that his time playing alongside DeChambeau gave him a clear understanding of what the power-hitter could have accomplished on the PGA Tour. This admission suggests that the gap between the tours was not as wide as some critics claimed. Koepka believes that if the LIV players had remained, the competition would have been fierce. "We all have a good feel how we would have fared on any tour," he noted. He believes Scheffler "would have won a lot of his golf tournaments," but he insists that the LIV contingent "would have put up a good fight."

The departure of major champions created a vacuum that Scheffler filled with historic consistency. Critics often point to the fact that three of Scheffler's four major wins occurred after the mass exodus of top talent. Koepka's comments provide a counter-narrative to the debate about the strength of his resume. He suggests that the presence of players like DeChambeau and himself would not have stopped Scheffler from winning, but it would have made the path much harder. The five-time major winner implies that the competition level on the PGA Tour would have remained elite had the split not occurred.

DeChambeau, who won the 2024 U.S. Open, is a central figure in this discussion. According to GolfMagic , DeChambeau's 2024 victory over Rory McIlroy by a single shot proves his game remains at the highest level. The two-time major winner now faces a new challenge as he plans his 2027 schedule on the DP World Tour. Unless the circuit alters its stance, DeChambeau faces a PGA Tour ban for at least 12 months following the LIV Golf collapse. New PGA Tour commissioner Brian Rolapp has expressed sentiments that make a return for DeChambeau in 2027 seem unlikely. This regulatory hurdle forces the American to look elsewhere for competitive play.

DeChambeau's New Path and Future Projects

DeChambeau is not sitting idle while waiting for a potential PGA Tour return. He has committed to an exemption on the DP World Tour, leveraging his U.S. Open status to pick and choose his schedule. GolfMagic reports that he will target lucrative Rolex Series events and tournaments surrounding the four men's majors. His journey begins in South Africa with the Nedbank Golf Challenge at Sun City, scheduled for 3-6 December. He is expected to follow this with the Dubai Desert Classic over 21-24 January. These events will serve as a tune-up for the major stretch in 2027.

Beyond tournament play, DeChambeau is expanding his footprint in the golf community through development projects. The Sun reported that the golfer announced a new initiative to design a championship course in his hometown of Clovis, California. Titled 'The Orchard,' the 18-hole facility will feature an on-site farmer's market and various community amenities. A signed statement from DeChambeau read, "There is a deep responsibility to give back to the region that provided us with so much." He intends for this course to serve as the initial one among many fully procured DeChambeau Designs. The Sun observed that the project seeks to transform the local area, in a signed statement from DeChambeau wrote, "It's time to make a better future for our next generation."

DeChambeau anticipates approval for the project within 18 months, with amenities like a driving range coming sooner. He expressed a broader hope for the facility, stating, "It is our hope that this will be a place where everyone in the world can come and enjoy the fruits of our labor here in the Central Valley." This community focus contrasts with the high-stakes professional golf world where Koepka and Scheffler compete. The golfer also maintains a strong digital presence, with his YouTube channel boasting over 3 million subscribers and multiple long-form videos posted monthly. The Sun noted that DeChambeau was one of LIV's poster boys before Saudi funding pulled out, sending the league into a deathspin. Despite the league's collapse, DeChambeau remains a dominant force, preparing for his next chapter on the DP World Tour starting in December.

articles.title: PGA Tour: England's Marco Penge grabs halfway lead at RSM Classic as big names battle to secure FedExCup future
articles.summary: Four players share the halfway lead at the RSM Classic, with only the top 100 players in the FedExCup standings after this week remaining fully exempt on the PGA Tour in 2027; watch the third round live on Saturday from 6pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Penge started the week 120th in the FedExCup standings and requiring at least a top-four finish to break inside the top 100 and guarantee full playing status on the PGA Tour in 2027.

A birdie-birdie finish saw Penge post a second-round 65 on the Stadium Course, one of two used at Sea Island Golf Club, leaving him in a four-way tie on nine under alongside Michael Thorbjornsen, China's Haotong Li and Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen.

"I'm in a bit of a weird situation," Penge admitted. "I missed seven or eight tournaments this year from injury and have some sort of medical exemption still, which I don't really know much about.

"I'm trying to feel like it's the last event, but at the same time knowing that I have maybe three or four, five tournaments to start next year that goes towards this year's ranking. There's a lot of us guys trying to keep our job this week and we're all trying to give it our all."

Thorbjornsen is already fully exempt on the PGA Tour next season, having won the Rocket Classic in August, while Li and Neergaard-Petersen - like Penge - started the week outside the top 100 in the standings.

A congested leaderboard sees a further five players a shot back, including Ryder Cup player Rasmsus Hojgaard as he looks to rise from 122 in the season standings, while England's Harry Hall heads into the weekend just two behind.

"It [FedExCup ranking] will always be in the back of your head a little bit," Hojgaard said. "There's still so much more golf to be played. I'm happy with the golf I played so far and hopefully I can keep doing that for the next few days."

Brooks Koepka, Presidents Cup star Jackson Koivun and past Ryder Cup captain Keegan Bradley are all four behind, while Christiaan Bezuidenhout - starting the week in 100th spot - is in tied-41st for the tournament and projected to drop down the standings.

A three-putt bogey on the final hole saw England's John Parry miss the cut by a shot, seeing him currently projected to finish in 101st spot, while eight-time PGA Tour winner Billy Horschel played his last three shots in four over and also made an early exit.

Those 51st to 60th after this week qualify for the first two Signature Events of 2027, while those who end between 101st and 125th on the PGA Tour only receive conditional status and be unable to feature in certain events.

Players outside the top 125 face a season on the Korn Ferry Tour or a trip to Q-School to earn their PGA Tour playing rights, with first-round leader Svensson entering the week in 135th spot.

articles.title: Official: Vikings Healthier vs 49ers, But Questionables Remain
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings wrapped up their practice week Friday with a final injury report for the 49ers game that includes an update on linebacker Blake Cashman...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings won 30-10 at Green Bay last weekend, improving their record to 7-2 on the season. They got the victory with five players ruled out: Blake Cashman, TJ Hockenson , Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Jauan Jennings and Kyler Murray.

One week later, they are set to get a few of those missing pieces back for a Sunday Night Football game against the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers down at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City.

This week, there were a bevy of question marks that needed answered on the injury front. On Friday, head coach Kevin O'Connell ruled out Addison, who had thumb surgery Monday but isn't going on IR, and Murray (hamstring). Neither of those were a surprise.

Minnesota Vikings Week final 11 injury report

However, cornerback Isaiah Rodgers (quad) was a new addition to the report on Thursday, One day later, he is questionable to play. Safety Jay Ward (knee) was limited all week, so his "questionable" status is less of a surprise.

The other seven injured players on the report, Cashman, Jennings, Van Ginkel, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Van Noy and Jeshaun Jones, have no game-status designation and are expected to be available.

Final #Vikings injury report OUT: WR Jordan Addison and QB Kyler Murray QUESTIONABLE: CB Isaiah Rodgers and S Jay Ward pic.twitter.com/c0rANSvTNV — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 20, 2026

Final #Vikings injury report OUT: WR Jordan Addison and QB Kyler Murray QUESTIONABLE: CB Isaiah Rodgers and S Jay Ward pic.twitter.com/c0rANSvTNV

Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 20, 2026

Cashman's concussion was diagnosed after the Week 9 loss to Buffalo, and forced him to sit out Week 10 in Green Bay. On Wednesday, O'Connell said he expected the linebacker to clear the concussion protocol that day. Cashman then practiced fully all three days this week.

He wears the green dot and plays a massive role in everything Brian Flores does on defense so having him back should make a big difference against arguably the most complete offensive team in the NFC. Through eight games, Cashman has 76 tackles and 4.5 sacks.

Over on offense, a calf injury has kept Jauan Jennings out of the last two games, including Sunday's win over the Packers. Like Cashman, he practiced fully all three days this week. On Thursday, he talked with reporters about facing his former team.

"I'm excited for every game. I mean, it's the San Francisco 49ers. It's my old team. I can't wait. It's always my guys for life (over there). Can't wait to see them." Alec Lewis – The Athletic

"I'm excited for every game. I mean, it's the San Francisco 49ers. It's my old team. I can't wait. It's always my guys for life (over there). Can't wait to see them."

Andrew Van Ginkel and Hockenson back too

Van Ginkel — who was limited Wednesday and Thursday but practiced as a full-participant Friday — has played in all nine games this season for the Minnesota Vikings. He has 8.5 sacks , 28 tackles, two forced fumbles and an interception.

He has a sack in seven of nine games, including 2.5 at Detroit on Nov. 1, and both of his forced fumbles came against Green Bay. O'Connell addressed the quad injury on Monday, the day after the win at Green Bay.

"He got looked at a little bit for kind of a leg, soft-tissue type of thing, but he's actually feeling pretty good. Expecting him to be able to work through the week, but more than likely will be limited early on, and we're hoping to have him." Lindsey Young – Vikings.com

"He got looked at a little bit for kind of a leg, soft-tissue type of thing, but he's actually feeling pretty good. Expecting him to be able to work through the week, but more than likely will be limited early on, and we're hoping to have him."

Hockenson and Ingram-Dawkins also sat out the Packers game, and neither carries a designation into Sunday. Hockenson has played in eight of the nine games this season and has 35 catches for 328 yards and three touchdowns.

He scored against Indianapolis on Oct. 25 and Detroit on Nov. 1, and his biggest game was 13 catches for 119 yards against Miami on Oct. 4. Van Noy, questionable a week ago, shook his injury designation too.

MN Vikings list Isaiah Rodgers, Jay Ward as questionable

Rodgers was mysteriously added to the injury report Thursday with a quad injury and was limited in practice both yesterday and today. He has played in all nine games this season and a major reason why Minnesota's pass defense has been so dominant.

O'Connell said Rodgers felt "pretty good," Goessling reported , and the team will see how he feels after post-practice treatment. Ward is the other one in doubt. The safety went into Green Bay without a designation, but he hasn't been a full participant in any practice this week.

Addison, who was questionable last week, is out this time following Monday's surgery, though he avoided IR . Murray is out again with his hamstring injury.

articles.title: DP World Tour Must Copy PGA Tour’s Koepka Fix To Keep Players Happy
articles.summary: The DP World Tour opens its doors to LIV players in 2027. Learn why adding extra field spots like the PGA Tour did with Brooks Koepka is the only way to save...
articles.body:
The DP World Tour has opened its gates for LIV Golf players to join in 2027. This move includes stars like Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, and Joaquin Niemann. Current members worry there will be no room left for them in the fields. The tour can fix this fear by copying the smart play the PGA Tour made with Brooks Koepka this year.

When Koepka returned from LIV, the PGA Tour did not take a spot from a regular member. Instead, they added three extra spots to every event where Koepka played. This simple change kept the peace while letting a star compete. The DP World Tour needs to do the same thing next season to avoid angering its own roster.

The PGA Tour faced a similar problem when Brooks Koepka decided to come back from the rival league. Tour officials knew that just letting him in could upset the players who stayed loyal. They needed a way to let him play without kicking anyone else out of the lineup. The solution was to grow the field size whenever he showed up.

In 2026, whenever Koepka joined a field, three additional spots were created for other competitors. Consequently, his participation did not displace any PGA Tour member from an event. His presence genuinely expanded competitive chances for other players.

Many golfers are scared that the return of big names will hurt their chances to play. When LIV Golf ceased operations, the question of where those players would go was huge. The DP World Tour supplied a full roster of ex‑LIV golfers competing in its events to address that query.

Current members now worry about insufficient field space, and the situation has intensified this concern. The fear is real because tournament fields have a hard cap on how many players can enter. If a new star takes a spot, someone else gets cut. To maintain member satisfaction, the DP World Tour should study the PGA Tour's approach to Brooks Koepka.

The most intelligent action taken by CEO Brian Rolapp and the PGA Tour is what the DP World Tour ought to copy. They realized that adding a player does not have to mean subtracting someone else. By adding spots, they turned a potential conflict into a benefit for the whole field. The DP World Tour could readily implement this strategy during the upcoming season.

Financial Stakes and the Need for Fair Play

Money plays a big role in why players want to stay or come back. Adopting a merit-based product caused total prize money to nearly double, increasing financial incentives. Tiger Woods observed this change, stating, "I can confidently say the PGA Tour is in the best position it has ever been."

However, the competition is much harder now. While still competing on LIV Golf, Koepka recognized Scheffler's dominance in 2024. "Scottie had a hell of a year," was the admission Koepka made in remarks covered by Yahoo Sports . Scheffler played 19 events and recorded seven wins, making all 19 cuts with 12 top-5 finishes.

With more money at stake, every spot in the field matters more. Jordan Spieth recognized how massive purse hikes created a ripple effect. Spieth acknowledged, "I would be lying if I said that we would have gone through this without LIV," alluding to the financial surge driven by the rival tour's spending.

The DP World Tour lists Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, and Joaquin Niemann for 2027.

The PGA Tour added three extra spots for every event Brooks Koepka played in 2026.

Total prize money on the PGA Tour has almost doubled since LIV Golf ceased operations.

Scottie Scheffler won seven times in 2024 and made every cut he played in.

articles.title: 49ers' Mike Evans ‘going in the right direction,' questionable to play vs. Vikings
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans was graded as questionable to play on Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, and was expected to practice ag...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) practiced Thursday for the first time since he left the 49ers' Oct. 19 win over the Washington Commanders. On Friday, asked how Evans felt coming out of it, head coach Kyle Shanahan said he was "a little sore" but "going in the right direction."

Evans was listed Thursday as a limited participant, and took part in individual drills during the open viewing portion of practice. He ran routes and caught passes at less than full speed. Shanahan said Evans will again be limited Friday during the 49ers' third practice at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado.

"We're all half-speed," Shanahan said, "so we'll keep him out of one period, and then he'll be limited in the rest."

San Francisco will make a decision on Evans' game status "probably tomorrow," according to Shanahan, depending on how he feels coming out of Friday's half-speed practice. The 49ers will have a final walkthrough Saturday morning before they fly to Mexico City for their Sunday night matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

General manager John Lynch said Thursday that the 49ers are being "extremely mindful" of the 33-year-old's long-term availability, and that he has "a chance" to play Sunday. "We're going to do what's in Mike's best interest so that when he's here, we can keep him out there," Lynch said on KNBR. "At least have the best chance of doing that."

If Evans does play, he'll no longer be the 49ers' oldest wideout. Trade deadline acquisition Keenan Allen (34) would run routes alongside Evans and tight end George Kittle (33), making for an ultra-experienced and tall primary receiving group for quarterback Brock Purdy . Evans is 6-foot-5, Allen is 6-foot-2 and Kittle is 6-foot-4.

"It's always good to have tall guys, but that only matters if they have really good hands," Shanahan said. "Fortunately, that's not the case with Mike and … Keenan."

More injury notes: Cornerback Renardo Green (back) came off the injury report Friday after being a full participant at Thursday's practice. Green exited the 49ers' last two games early, and he was questionable entering last Sunday's contest against the Dallas Cowboys, but he has no injury designation this week. On Monday, Shanahan said he believed Green was just dealing with back tightness.

San Francisco's other starting cornerback, Deommodore Lenoir, was a full participant all week after being limited last week by a foot issue. Lenoir, who played through the injury Sunday against Dallas, allowed 10 catches for 134 yards and three touchdowns on 17 targets.

After the game, Lenoir said: "I don't want to make that a problem. … I told everybody I was 100%. So, you know, I got to be better."

Linebacker Dre Greenlaw is questionable with a neck injury that he picked up this week. After not practicing Wednesday, Greenlaw was a limited participant Thursday and Friday. Shanahan indicated the linebacker is dealing with a nerve issue in his neck: "Hoping he'll be all right. You never know with nerves and stuff with (the) neck, but hoping it continues to go the right direction."

Other 49ers who were hit with the questionable tag: CB Upton Stout (shoulder, neck), RB Jordan James (calf), DT CJ West (knee), CB Nate Hobbs (adductor), DE Khalid Kareem (ankle), QB Mac Jones (illness) and LB Luke Gifford (chest). West and Hobbs remained on injured reserve and would need to be activated and placed back on the 53-man roster to play Sunday.

articles.title: Driver Adjustments Shift Aim, Cost Strokes For Amateurs
articles.summary: PGA Tour putting coach Stephen Sweeney reveals how driver and putter setup errors force players to aim right, costing strokes on the greens.
articles.body:
Many golfers believe fixing their driver requires complex swing changes or expensive new equipment. A recent analysis shows that setup adjustments often yield better results than mechanical overhauls. PGA Tour putting coach Stephen Sweeney identified specific alignment issues that cause players to miss targets consistently. These errors start before the club even moves. The focus shifts from what is in the bag to how the body aligns with the ball.

Stephen Sweeney broke down two critical errors that ruin short-game performance. The first mistake involves eye position relative to the ball. "Where your eyes are right now, I tend to see if players' eyes are inside the ball line; they tend to look out to the right," Sweeney said. The arrangement forces the putter to travel from inside to out, creating a path that works for full swings but hinders short putts. The fix requires hinging at the waist more to reach a "tabletop" position. Golfers should keep two putter heads of space from the ball to the toe line and bend forward until eyes sit directly over the golf ball.

The second error involves a right-aligned putter face at address. Because the eyes were looking from the inside, the writer subconsciously aimed the face right and tried to pull the ball back to the line. Once the eyes moved on top of the ball, lining up the face became much easier. Sweeney showed a clever trick using a phone to check the aim. "Just go ahead and set up and aim your putter face," Sweeney said. "If I go ahead and set the back of my phone to your putter face, and you come back and look down that line, you can see the face aimed on the right edge." This visual confirmation helps players understand their true alignment versus their perceived alignment.

Correcting these issues changes the entire stroke mechanics. Confidence returned, and more putts dropped after the writer made these two adjustments. Sweeney explained the mechanics clearly: "As the putter goes back, the putter is moving a little on the inside — but pretty square to where you aimed it." Equipment like the TaylorMade Qi4D driver or Ping irons listed in Golf Monthly reports can enhance performance, but they cannot fix a broken setup. A player might have the best driver in the world, yet if their eyes are inside the line, the ball will miss the target. The relationship between setup and result remains the most consistent factor in golf.

Alignment errors often go unnoticed because they feel natural to the player. Sweeney's observations highlight how a small tilt in the eyes changes the entire path of the club. When eyes sit inside the ball, the brain compensates by aiming the face right. This creates a disconnect between where the player thinks they are aiming and where the club is actually pointing. The phone trick is an objective check that removes guesswork. It reveals the true face angle without relying on feel. Many amateurs struggle with three-putting because they fight a path that doesn't match their aim.

Professional players spend hours refining their setup to ensure consistency. Sam, a golf industry veteran with 15 years of experience, notes that equipment choices must match the player's swing. Sam's current bag includes a TaylorMade Qi4D 8° driver and Ping Blueprint T irons, but his success stems from understanding how these tools work together. Winning the club championship three times in succession from 2015-2017 at North Hants Golf Club shows the value of a solid foundation. Even with high-end gear, a poor setup leads to poor results. The data from Yahoo Sports confirms that fixing the setup fixes the stroke.

Complex swing thoughts often lead to paralysis. Sweeney's approach focuses on two tiny fixes that save strokes without requiring a complete swing rebuild. The "tabletop" position ensures the eyes are over the ball, eliminating the need for the brain to compensate. This simple adjustment aligns the body with the target line naturally. The phone trick provides immediate feedback, allowing players to see their errors in real time. These methods rely on geometry rather than feel.

Golfers who struggle with consistency often overlook the basics. They look for a miracle swing change instead of checking their alignment. The report from Yahoo Sports proves that small changes yield big results. After merely those two adjustments, the author felt as though they were a brand new player on the greens. This transformation did not require new clubs or a new coach. It required a shift in perspective and a willingness to check the facts. The mechanics remain the same for every player, regardless of skill level. Sweeney's advice applies to everyone from the amateur to the tour pro.

articles.title: LPGA Tour: Charley Hull in CME Group Tour Championship contention as A Lim Kim fires hole-in-one to grab halfway lead
articles.summary: Charley Hull is four off the halfway lead as she chases a second CME Group Tour Championship title; A Lim Kim three clear after making an ace at the par-three 16th during her second round; live coverage continues on Saturday from 4pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Kim holed her tee shot with a seven iron at the 168-yard par-three 16th, with the Korean adding seven birdies and a lone bogey in a round-of-the-day 64 at Tiburon Golf Club.

The former US Women's Open champion was tied at the top of the leaderboard until her stunning ace and a birdie at the par-five next, which moved Kim to 15 under and three clear of back-to-back defending champion Jeeno Thitikul.

Thitikul posted five birdies in a seven-hole stretch on her back nine during a second-round 67, putting her in the final group on Saturday, with Hull a further shot back in a share of third after matching the world No 2's score.

Yuri Yoshida, Ina Yoon, Yan Liu, Jenny Bae and Auston Kim complete the logjam on 11 under alongside Hull, who posted five birdies in a blemish-free round as the 2016 champion looks to win the CME Group Tour Championship for a second time.

"I've just been pretty solid the last couple days, and hopefully I can replicate that on the weekend," Hull admitted. "I didn't actually hole that many putts, but I hit it quite close."

Only the top 60 players in the season-long Race to the CME Globe get to tee it up in Florida, with world No 1 Nelly Korda six off the halfway lead as she chase the $4m (£3.04m) winner's cheque.

"I'm just not hitting it as solid as I would like," Korda explained. "I have a little bit of a two-way miss going and that's kind of death for any golfer - you're not very confident over the shot.

"I'm just trying to get myself one key that I'm just going to go with for the whole week. I have yet to figure it out - hopefully the weekend brings me some luck!"

England's Lottie Woad dropped to tied-22nd after a two-under 70, while Ireland's Leona Maguire heads into the weekend sharing 42nd after rounds of 70 and 71 over the first two days.

Who will win the CME Group Tour Championship? Watch throughout the weekend live on Sky Sports. Live coverage continues Saturday from 4pm on Sky Sports Golf. Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract .

articles.title: LPGA Tour: South Korea's A-Lim Kim hits hole-in-one on way to three-shot lead at Tour Championship
articles.summary: South Korea's A-Lim Kim aces the par-three 16th on her way to claiming a three-shot lead after the second round of CME Group Tour Championship.
articles.body:
CME Group Tour Championship - round two leaderboard

15 AL Kim (Kor); -12 J Thitikul (Tha); -11 C Hull (Eng), J Bae (US), A Kim (US), Y Yoshida (Jap), I Yoon (Kor), Y Liu (Chn)

Selected others: -10 M Stark (Swe); -9 N Korda (US); -7 P Roussin-Bouchard (Fra), L Woad (Eng); -3 L Maguire (Ire)

South Korea's A-Lim Kim aced the par-three 16th hole on her way to claiming a three-shot lead after the second round of CME Group Tour Championship.

The 31-year-old held a share of the lead after the first round at Tiburon Golf Club in Florida but is out on her own after shooting a superb 64 on Friday.

Kim made seven birdies and one eagle, the hole-in-one on 16, with a solitary bogey to head into the weekend 15 under and with a great chance of claiming the $4m (£3.05m) top prize.

"When I hit, after, I felt it was a little strong, but hit the pin and then went in," Kim said of her hole-in-one, the third of her career. "I think it was luck."

On the potential to win millions on Sunday, she added: "Money is money. It has not bothered me. I think winning is more important for me."

England's Charley Hull is one of six players four strokes back in a tie for third, with Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand one shot better off in second.

Hull posted a blemish-free 67, with five birdies, to keep herself right in the mix in a stacked field that contains the top 60 in this season's points list.

World number one Nelly Korda, who will qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame if she wins on Sunday, also produced a five-under 67 and heads into round three tied for 11th on nine under.

With an $11m purse on offer, Korda would also break Annika Sorenstam's career earnings record if she finishes in sixth place or better.

The Swede amassed 10 major titles and earned $22,583,694 during a storied career before retiring in 2008, with Korda now just under $160,000 behind that mark.

articles.title: Adani power project in Satara: ‘Nod covers 4 villages, excavation on at 5th’
articles.summary: Satara Adani Tarali pumped storage project faces claims of excavation in Sawarghar village not listed in the environmental clearance; MPCB probes approvals and NBWL status.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Amid a row over work on Adani Green Energy Ltd’s (AGEL) 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project beginning in Satara’s Patan taluka despite lack of approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), the state forest department’s honorary wildlife warden for the district has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway in Sawarghar village, which was not listed on the environmental clearance (EC) granted by the Union forest ministry on Feb 11 last year.The honorary wildlife warden, Rohan Bhate, said the EC specified only four villages that stand to be affected—Nivade, Tondoshi, Kalambe and Jalu—in the district.A spokesperson from Adani Group said the EC covers the four villages as well as Dafalwadi, and the company later purchased private land in Sawarghar to set up temporary accommodation for workers. The company said such an accommodation was included in the project layout approval from Central Electricity Authority. It said the project has all the relevant clearances and initial works are in progress at the site.The Tarali project, estimated at Rs 5,675 crore, is planned over 150.7 hectares of private land.In his letter to MPCB member-secretary Rahul Rekhawar, Bhate claimed that the activity in Sawarghar did not have the required EC and NBWL’s approval, and sought urgent intervention and an independent investigation.Rekhawar confirmed that MPCB has received Bhate’s letter and said it is investigating the allegations.Amol Satpute, MPCB sub-regional officer in Satara, said a team from the pollution regulator inspected the Sawarghar site on Friday, where excavation was underway. Satpute said when officials questioned the site supervisor, they were told the developer was levelling land to set up a labour camp for the Tarali project. He said a report would be submitted to higher authorities.Bhate said the situation raised questions about the geographical scope and validity of the EC in relation to the work being carried out at Sawarghar. He questioned whether MPCB had verified that the proponent had obtained environmental and wildlife clearances for all land parcels involved before issuing the mandatory ‘consent to establish’ (CTE) that allows construction to begin. He said MPCB cannot distance itself from responsibility because the CTE stage is a crucial regulatory checkpoint.Bhate requested an immediate site inspection and preparation of an official panchnama by MPCB officials to document the extent of excavation and construction, the machinery deployed, and the exact location of the work. He said if any excavation or construction is found to have started without statutory approvals, authorities should register the appropriate offence and initiate legal proceedings against responsible individuals and project authorities.He also asked MPCB to determine whether activity at Sawarghar is covered by the Feb 11, 2025, EC and whether all applicable environmental permissions for that specific location have been obtained. In addition, he sought verification of whether prior approval from the NBWL’s standing committee was secured wherever legally required.Bhate said the proposed project falls within the deemed eco-sensitive zone of Koyna wildlife sanctuary and the Sahyadri tiger reserve, making strict scrutiny under environmental and wildlife protection provisions essential. He requested that the matter be assigned to an impartial higher-level authority for an independent inquiry rather than being examined only by officials linked to project clearances. Pending verification, he asked for directions to prevent any further unauthorised excavation or construction at the site.Sources said AGEL has not yet complied with the stop-work order issued on Nov 13 by Satpute, in his capacity as the Satara division’s deputy conservator of forests, for starting work on the project without NBWL’s approval. Adani Group had earlier said the proposal had been submitted to NBWL. articles.title: Sean McVay has at least one positive injury update
articles.summary: Kobie Turner is set to return after the bye when Rams host Packers
articles.body:
While Puka Nacua's potentially season-ending surgery and possible ending of his tenure with the Los Angeles Rams has dominated the headlines, there is at least one silver lining from Sean McVay's injury updates this week.

Defensive tackle Kobie Turner is likely set to return following the bye in an all-important NFC clash against the Green Bay Packers. Turner suffered a groin injury back in Week 6—LA's first game against the Arizona Cardinals. Since then, Myles Garrett has also returned to health and has wrecked shop in company with Aaron Donald. Turner should add even more juice to an already formidable front.

The Rams won't get back Poona Ford this year. While opposing offenses have not gashed the Rams on the ground, Turner is an important part of the run defense and should help offset what is a significant long-term loss.

But the news ahead of the Green Bay game was not all positive. Davante Adams, who was rumored to potentially be ready to face off against his former team, will likely not be ready to return in time per McVay. Adams is week-to-week and will be evaluated after the Packers game.

And it's a similar story for tight end Terrance Ferguson. The Rams will activate the former second-round pick before his 21-day window closes, which prevents him from being shutdown for the remainder of the season. He won't be able to return to play in this time frame, however, and will take a spot on the 53-man roster.

The Rams can't really afford to lose to the Packers on Wednesday night. In addition to their NFC West rivals, they are indirectly competing against the entire NFC North in the playoff picture. The race against Green Bay could come down the wire. This is an opportunity for LA to bolster their own position while directly putting the Packers at a disadvantage.

Kobie Turner is a welcome reinforcement for that game. Not having Davante Adams nor Terrance Ferguson in time is an unfortunate development.

LA still needs to find a way to get the job done.
